subject: RFP question: archive harvestability, tamper-evidence, and export SLA
messages:
From: Tom Reilly <tom.reilly@globex.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Globex Security Team <security-questions@globex.com>
Date: Sun, 30 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: RFP question: archive harvestability & tamper-evidence

Hi Laura / Marissa,

We're working through the audit/logging section of the RFP and need specifics around three areas:

1) Tamper evidence / immutability: does Redwood provide cryptographic tamper-detection for audit logs (e.g., signed checkpoints, WORM storage, or HSM-backed manifests)?
2) Exportability / harvestability: what export formats do you support for bulk forensic exports (NDJSON, CSV, Parquet)? Can we request exports to our S3 bucket (cross-account)?
3) Export SLA / latency: if we request a 90-day activity export for an internal investigation, how long until we receive a forensic-grade bundle and a signed manifest?

Also please call out whether exported data includes full request/response payloads or only metadata. We're scoping retention and chain-of-custody requirements for regulated customers.

Appreciate concise, call-out style answers so we can fold them into the RFP appendix.

Thanks,
Tom
Tom Reilly
Senior Security PM – Globex Corporation
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Reilly <tom.reilly@globex.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 31 Aug 2026 08:34:00 -0700
Subject: Re: RFP question: archive harvestability & tamper-evidence

Tom — thanks for the clear list. See a summarized response below and attached playbook (audit-export-playbook.pdf) with sample manifests. I'm happy to expand any section.

1) Tamper evidence / immutability
- Internal store: append-only audit log with continuous hashing checkpoints (SHA-256 chain) recorded every hour for high-traffic tenants.
- Signed checkpoints: for Dedicated and Private deployments we provide optional HSM-backed signed checkpoints (FIPS 140-2 compatible) and periodic signed manifests.
- WORM: Private deployments can be configured with WORM-compliant object stores; hosted customers can request export snapshots with signed manifests for external archival.

2) Exportability / formats & delivery
- Supported bulk export formats: NDJSON (preferred), gzipped CSV, Parquet (analytics-friendly).
- Delivery: exports delivered via presigned S3 PUT to customer bucket, direct S3 cross-account puts for enterprise customers, or secure HTTPS bundle download behind pre-authenticated link.
- Export contents: by default, audit exports contain metadata (timestamps, request ids, model id, token counts, response status), and full request/response bodies are available only when the customer has opted into request-body logging (DPA addendum required).

3) Export SLA / latency
- Standard extraction: up to 30 days of logs -> delivery within 2–6 hours depending on tenant size; 90-day full exports typically <8 hours under normal load.
- Forensic/accelerated windows: we offer an expedited service (reserved capacity + expedited IO) for guaranteed delivery within 4 hours for critical investigations (requires ordering within SLA window; see playbook).
- Signed manifests: each export includes a SHA-256 manifest and an optional RedHat-style detached signature (sample-manifest.sig attached). For Dedicated/Private, manifests can be signed with customer-provided keys via KMS/HSM integration.

Additional notes:
- Chain-of-custody: export metadata includes exporter id, export request id, UTC timestamp, checksums, and storage location. We provide a checklist for ingest into customer evidence systems.
- Retention: hosted audit logs default retention is 90 days; configurable up to 365 days for mid-market customers. Private deployments support customer-defined retention policies up to multi-year (7+ yrs) as required by compliance.
- Redaction: Redwood supports configurable redaction at ingest and dual-stream exports (one redacted, one original) for customers who need both for analysis and downstream archival; original payloads require explicit agreement.

See attached: audit-export-playbook.pdf (runbook), sample-manifest.sig (signature example). Also linking our export schema (log-schema-v2.json) in a follow-up if helpful.

If you'd like, Marissa and Karthik can join a 30-minute call to walk the RFP reviewers through the playbook next week.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Head of Enterprise Sales – Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: RFP question: archive harvestability & tamper-evidence

Thanks Laura — helpful. A couple of quick clarifications for our compliance team:

- For hosted customers that opt into full request/response logging, are request/response bodies stored encrypted-at-rest with customer-managed keys?
- On the dual-stream export (redacted + original) — can exported manifests clearly mark which bundle is redacted vs original and include a redaction audit log?
- If we request a 90-day export to our S3 bucket, will the export include a signed manifest that we can validate independently (i.e., public key for signature verification)?

If you can confirm those three items we'll mark the item as 'accepted' in the RFP.

Tom
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Reilly <tom.reilly@globex.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 2 Sep 2026 16:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: RFP question: archive harvestability & tamper-evidence

Tom — short answers below, and attaching log-schema-v2.json for field-level clarity.

- Encryption & CMKs: yes. For hosted tenants that opt-in to request-body storage, data is encrypted at rest; for enterprise customers we support Bring Your Own Key (BYOK) via KMS integrations (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, or customer HSM). Keys are rotated on a configurable schedule; exports are delivered encrypted and can be wrapped with your CMK on request.

- Dual-stream manifests & redaction audit: exported bundles include a top-level manifest that lists bundle ids, whether a bundle is redacted or original, checksums for each file, and a redaction-audit.json that enumerates redaction causes (rule id, timestamp, operator). This is included in all dual-stream exports.

- Signature verification: signed manifests use a standard detached signature (RFC 5656 style). We can provide a public key for external verification or configure signature verification via customer KMS on Private/Dedicated. The sample-manifest.sig shows the detached signature format; the playbook documents verification steps.

Next steps: if Globex wants the BYOK + HSM-signed manifests path, we can scope this as a dedicated compliance package on the deal (DEAL-2026-0042). Marissa is looped to prepare a short statement of work and costs.

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick call.

Laura Bennett
Head of Enterprise Sales – Redwood Inference
